chunks: So we said, “May Allah set you right, then one handful suffices for the face and one handful for the arm?” He said: “Yes, if you do it thoroughly; and two handfuls cover all of that entirely.”
(212) 61 As for the hadith that he narrated—

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Ziyad and al-'Abbas ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“Wudu (ablution) once is an obligation; twice, no reward is given; and the third is an innovation.”

His statement, “and twice, no reward is given,” means: if he believes that the two are obligatory, he is not rewarded for them. But if he believes that they are sunnah (prophetic tradition), then he is rewarded for that. And that which indicates what we have said...

key_terms.فَرْضٌ: that which is obligatory and legally required
key_terms.لَا يُؤْجَرُ: no reward is given for it in the stated circumstance
key_terms.ٱلْغُرْفَةُ: a handful or scoop of water used in washing
key_terms.ٱلْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before acts of worship

ai.seo_question: How many times should each part be washed in wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling on the number of washes in wudu (ablution). It states that a single washing is the obligatory minimum, while a second may be done and can be rewarded if understood as sunnah (prophetic tradition), but a third washing is considered bid'ah (innovation).
